title: Bot restarted on this PC
what: Paper bot back online with Task Scheduler + heartbeat watchdog.

title: Selective beats volume
what: Pushing trade volume broke the bot; target became ~2 selective trades/day.

title: 6 close-handler data bugs fixed
what: Trades were being recorded wrong on close; fixed and verified with a swarm.

title: Leverage double-count bug
what: P&L was multiplied by leverage twice for months. Corrected: the bot was actually net negative, shorts +$667 vs longs -$796.

title: Website back live
what: crazyonsol.online had been frozen 3 months by one build error.

title: Fees + early exits were the leak
what: ~9 bps round trip on large notionals ate ~13% of the risk budget per trade.

title: Tailwind gate
what: Looked like 70% win rate; on entry-time-safe data it was a coin flip. Not built.

title: Co-pilot analyst suite
what: eye / call / scan tools that instrument the owner's own reads instead of predicting.

title: Plain-language dashboard
what: Headline-first status page; 278 GB of junk removed from this PC.

title: 45-day zero-trade drought explained
what: The entry gate blocked 100% of trades. It was right on the evidence, but froze learning; probes added.

title: Liquidation clustering is real (BTC/SOL)
what: Survives a local-rate null at ~1/4 of the naive headline. It signals cascade RISK, not direction.

title: No AI agent predicts price
what: 8,340 bot decisions graded forward: skipping everything beat every agent. Value is only in risk vetoes and exits.

title: 2-day AI outage
what: Login expired + a $1 per-call cap silently degraded the bot. Now alarmed on the dashboard.

title: Hivemind + chief analyst
what: Every voice per coin with report cards; Opus chief reads every 4h; all graded forward.

title: Move SIZE is forecastable
what: Volatility forecast beat the naive guess in 22/22 test periods. Direction is not forecastable (0 of ~98 tests).

title: WAGMI Terminal v2
what: Hyperliquid-style trading terminal: watchlist, chart 15m-1W, planner, scanner, tabs.

title: Your plans graded 3 ways
what: Plan as written, the bot's suggested levels (Opus review), and the bot paper-managing it.

title: 2x stop / 0.5R target / 48h recipe
what: Laptop red team withdrew it: the gain was fee arithmetic. Only 'tighter stops hurt' stands.

title: 50-day pullback as a trade
what: 724 cases: random dates did as well. The 50d average stopped acting as support after 2024.

title: The bot's hidden filter looks right
what: Signals it silently drops would have lost money (supported, not yet proven). Keep it.

title: Liquidation clusters as magnets
what: Aug study: reached LESS than random; Oct: +8 pts. Pooled +3.4, CI spans zero. Proximity, not magnetism.

title: Tests were writing into the live bot
what: ~4,000 writes, including wiping the bot's memory file. Now blocked.

title: Following every Syndicate call loses
what: 188 graded calls with a strict exit: median -53%. Nobody beat random under that rule.

title: Some Syndicate callers stand out at 1.5x
what: Selling all at 1.5x: @DUBI_CH 17/18 hit, +40%/call. Found after trying 3 exit rules; survives that correction only by a thin margin, so the forward test on new calls decides.

title: Claude trade ideas + call verdicts
what: Opus proposes swing trades twice a day; Sonnet judges every Syndicate call; both graded.

title: Laptop must corroborate bot changes
what: Owner rule: no trading change stays live without the laptop's red-teamed verdict.

title: Crowded longs = bigger days (held up on 156 new coins)
what: Days when a coin's funding is in the top 20% move more than usual for that coin. Re-checked on 156 coins the test never saw: still ~+5% bigger. Size and stop width only - not direction.

title: Trailing exit beats a fixed target
what: Laptop's own simulation had two bugs; done right, trailing is not better (-0.02 to -0.04R).

title: ~200 plans to judge a trader
what: Below ~50 plans a winning streak can't be told from luck.

title: Logging open interest for all perps
what: HL keeps no history of OI/premium/impact prices; every 15-min snapshot is now saved.

title: Where the bot's money comes from
what: Real ledger: trailing stops + TP2 = +$1,161 on 8.5% of trades; the AI exit agent's early closes = -$845 on 47%. Being red-teamed.

title: 'Exit agent is the leak'
what: Era confound (June vs autumn). Its early closes come out roughly neutral. Nothing changed.

title: Long-side losses were June-July
what: Shorts +$668 in June; longs -$796 in Jun-Jul. Already fixed in late July. Code is symmetric.

title: Bot stays mostly flat
what: No blocked trade type shows an edge after fees. Staying flat is right until one does.

title: Grader saw only 4h of a 12h window
what: Blocked-signal grading fixed; ledger now logs R correctly plus stops and targets.

title: The bot's final confidence number doesn't pick better trades
what: On 176 real trades a higher cut on the final confidence only meant fewer trades; shuffled did as well. The live entry floor uses a different number - not tested yet.

title: Crowded longs: stops hit a bit more often (held up on 156 new coins)
what: When a coin's funding is in the top 20%, a normal stop gets hit ~2.4 pts more often - re-checked on 156 coins the test never saw, with the exact flag the terminal uses. Size down a little. Not direction.

title: Safe leverage was ~15% too generous
what: It came from too few bad days to see the true worst ones. The terminal now shows the corrected, safer number.

title: Bot-down alerts reach your phone
what: In September a 3-day crash was detected but nobody saw it. Now 'bot down' or 'AI degraded' goes to your Telegram Saved Messages.

title: Laptop crunches data on its own, hourly
what: No Claude needed: archives every coin's candles, funding and open interest (830k bars, 169 coins) and keeps the tests' counts current.

title: Don't chase small-cap breakouts (in history; forward test running)
what: Corrected on 164 coins: a small cap breaking its 20-day high tends to FALL vs peers over 1-7 days (8%+ above: about -15% in 3 days). Avoid longs there. Shorting it is not proven.

title: Counter-trend entries lose more (RETRACTED)
what: Retracted 10-12: momentum had been measured at the trade CLOSE, so it contained the outcome. Measured at the real entry, the win-rate gap is gone.

title: Syndicate moonbags: can't tell yet
what: 200 calls, 31 days: most lose about half; whether keeping a slice beats selling all is unanswerable until ~3x more calls. Missing-price calls (likely rugs) flip the sign.

title: Picking Syndicate winners at call time
what: 300 calls, 17 call-time stats, prereg + holdout: nothing picks the 1.5x runners. Small/thin coins die more (70% vs 35%) but win as often. Top 5% of calls = 60% of upside.

title: Buying every meme call, any exit rule
what: 413 corrected calls, before fees: every exit target (1.5x/2x/3x) lands at about -9 to -11% per call at 24h, 7d and 14d (statistically clear at all three); holding about -45%; ~1 in 5 coins dies. The target is not the lever - the assets are. 10x runners real but rare.
